key_insight: The paper extends lattice Boltzmann methods from uniform Cartesian meshes to general orthogonal coordinates, enabling efficient Navier–Stokes simulation on nonuniform clustered grids while preserving collide-and-stream simplicity and Galilean invariance.
engineering_relevance: This makes LBM more practical for boundary layers, multiscale flows, and other problems where local grid refinement is needed to reduce cost without sacrificing near-wall resolution.
method: Use a coordinate transformation to formulate LBM in general orthogonal coordinates.
Derive equilibrium moments and geometric force terms with Chapman–Enskog analysis, including metric factors and their spatial derivatives.
Apply the framework across collision models; the central-moments MRT version is reported as most robust.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on multiple benchmark flow problems and case studies, including efficient boundary-layer simulation and orthogonal curvilinear-grid tests.
watch_item: Implementation requires careful handling of metric-dependent forcing and correction terms, especially normal-velocity gradients, to avoid losing accuracy or robustness.
paper_title: Lattice Boltzmann Methods for Navier-Stokes Equations in General Orthogonal Coordinates for Efficient Flow Simulations using Nonuniform Clustered Grids
